candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: permitAudience

Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. candidates.label: followee

Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: targetUrl

candidates.label: audience

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation

candidates.label: targetName

candidates.label: claimInterpreter

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy

candidates.label: claimReviewed

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter

candidates.label: appearance

candidates.label: isBasedOnUrl

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin

candidates.label: actionProcess
candidates.comment: An action process relation between an action and the step-by-step instructions or method by which it was carried out. Also called execution method, procedure, how-to guide. Examples: "A 'bake cake' action's action process is a recipe.", "A 'repair car' action's action process is a repair manual."

candidates.label: actionPlatform
candidates.comment: An action platform relation between an entry point and the high-level digital platform(s) where the associated action can be performed. Also called execution platform, supported environment, operating system. Examples: "A web application's action platform is 'WebPlatform'.", "A mobile app's action platform is 'iOS'."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: howPerformed
candidates.comment: A performance method relation between a medical procedure and a description of how it is carried out. Also called procedure steps, method of procedure, execution details. Examples: "A medical procedure has a description of how it is performed.", "The surgery details how it is performed.", "This procedure outlines how it is performed."

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: performTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to execute instructions or a direction, excluding preparation time. Also called execution time, active time, task duration. Examples: A recipe's instructions have a perform time of 'PT30M'. A DIY project direction has a perform time of 'PT2H'. A workout routine has a perform time of 'PT45M'. Distinct from prepTime, which is the time to prepare supplies.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: legislationTransposes
candidates.comment: A transposition relation between two pieces of legislation, where one fulfills the objectives of the other through implementation measures. Also called: transposes, implements directive, fulfills objectives of. Examples: "Member State Law legislationTransposes EU Directive", "Regional Act legislationTransposes National Regulation", "Local Ordinance legislationTransposes State Mandate". Distinct from legislationEnsuresImplementationOf, which implies modifying national legislations to avoid contradiction, rather than fulfilling objectives.

candidates.label: causeOf

Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: infectiousAgent
candidates.comment: A causative agent relation between an infectious disease and the specific microorganism or pathogen that causes it. Also called causative organism, pathogen, disease agent, etiological agent. Examples: Influenza has an infectiousAgent of 'Influenza virus'. Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent of 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Malaria has an infectiousAgent of 'Plasmodium falciparum'. Distinct from infectiousAgentClass, which specifies the *type* of agent (e.g., bacteria, virus).

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: relatedDrug
candidates.comment: A related drug relation between a drug and other drugs that are similar or commonly prescribed alternatives. Also called alternative drug, similar medication, related medication. Examples: "A pain reliever has a related drug 'ibuprofen'.", "An antidepressant has a related drug 'SSRI'.", "A blood pressure medication has a related drug 'diuretic'."

candidates.label: free
candidates.comment: A free relation indicating whether a publication event, item, or place is accessible without cost. Also called: no charge, complimentary, gratis. Examples: "Online Article Publication" free "true", "Concert Event" free "false", "Public Park Access" free "true".

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: relatedAnatomy
candidates.comment: A related anatomy relation between superficial anatomy and other anatomical structures or systems connected to it. Also called associated anatomy, connected to anatomy. Examples: "The skin of the forearm has related anatomy 'radius bone'.", "The superficial muscles of the back have related anatomy 'vertebral column'.", "The scalp has related anatomy 'cranium'."

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

relations.definition: Exists within the boundaries of a specified geographic area
relations.embedding_query_text: located in: Exists within the boundaries of a specified geographic area

Ukraine attacks Russian oil refineries -> Yaroslavl

chosen_property.label: locatedInAdministrativeArea
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating that a military attack event is located within the boundaries of an administrative area.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly links a MilitaryAttackEvent to an AdministrativeArea as its location; 'containedInPlace' applies to Places, not events.

candidates.label: polygon
candidates.comment: A geographical attribute defining a polygon as a series of space-delimited points that enclose an area, with identical start and end points. Also called geographic boundary, area coordinates, shape definition. Examples: A geo shape has a polygon '30 10 40 40 20 40 10 20 30 10'. A region is defined by a polygon '50 0 60 30 40 30 50 0'. The park boundary is a polygon 'lat1 lon1 lat2 lon2 lat3 lon3 lat1 lon1'.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: shippingDestination
candidates.comment: The specified geographical region or regions where shipping is available or targeted. Also called delivery destination, shipping region, target delivery area. Examples: `Shipping Rate Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: US Postal Codes 90000-90210`, `Offer Shipping Details` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: European Union`, `Delivery Time Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: North America`. Distinct from `shippingOrigin`, which is where the shipment comes from.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geoTouches
candidates.comment: A geo touches relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one boundary point but no interior points. Also called: borders, adjoins, meets at boundary. Examples: "Country A" geo touches "Country B", "Property Line 1" geo touches "Property Line 2", "Lake Shore" geo touches "Land Mass". Distinct from geoIntersects, which can share interior points.

candidates.label: box
candidates.comment: A textual representation of a rectangular area defined by two points (lower and upper corners) for a geo shape. Also called: bounding box, geographic box, spatial extent. Examples: "GeoShape 'Region A' box '34 -118 36 -116'", "GeoShape 'Area B' box '40.71 -74.01 40.78 -73.95'."

Ukraine attacks Russian oil refineries -> 700km

chosen_property.label: distanceFromTarget
chosen_property.definition: The spatial distance between a military attack event and its target location.
chosen_property.justification: The 'geoRadius' applies to GeoCircle, not events; a new property is needed to capture the distance from the attack's target.

candidates.label: geoDisjoint
candidates.comment: A geo disjoint relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places have no points in common and are entirely disconnected. Also called: separate from, not overlapping, unconnected. Examples: "Country 'USA'" geo disjoint "Country 'China'", "Island 'Hawaii'" geo disjoint "Continent 'Europe'", "Building 'A'" geo disjoint "Building 'B'". Distinct from geoIntersects, which has at least one point in common.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: geoRadius
candidates.comment: A geo radius relation between a geo circle and its approximate radial distance from the center. Also called: circle radius, geographic radius, extent. Examples: "Search Area GeoCircle" geo radius "5000 meters", "Weather Alert Zone" geo radius "10 miles", "GPS Accuracy Circle" geo radius "10 feet".

candidates.label: geoEquals
candidates.comment: A geo equals relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places are topologically identical, sharing the same interior and boundary without intersecting each other's exterior. Also called: identical to, same location as, equivalent geometry. Examples: "City Boundary A" geo equals "City Boundary B (updated)", "Park Outline (old)" geo equals "Park Outline (new)", "Country Shape (vector)" geo equals "Country Shape (raster)".

candidates.label: geoCrosses
candidates.comment: A geo crosses relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places intersect, sharing some but not all interior points, and their intersection has a lower dimension than at least one of them. Also called: intersects, traverses, cuts across. Examples: "River 'Mississippi'" geo crosses "State 'Missouri'", "Road 'Route 66'" geo crosses "City 'Chicago'", "Flight Path" geo crosses "Mountain Range".

candidates.label: longitude
candidates.comment: A longitude relation between geographic coordinates or a place and its longitudinal value. Also called: geographic longitude, east-west coordinate, meridian position. Examples: "Eiffel Tower longitude 2.2945", "Statue of Liberty longitude -74.0445", "Mount Everest longitude 86.9250".

candidates.label: geoIntersects
candidates.comment: A geo intersects relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one common point. Also called: overlaps with, touches, crosses. Examples: "River 'Thames'" geo intersects "City 'London'", "Road 'Main Street'" geo intersects "Park 'Central Park'", "Country 'USA'" geo intersects "Country 'Canada'". Distinct from geoDisjoint, which has no points in common.

candidates.label: wheelbase
candidates.comment: A wheelbase dimension relation between a vehicle and a quantitative value, specifying the distance between its front and rear wheel centers. Also called wheel distance, axle distance, inter-axle distance. Examples: Sedan wheelbase 2.7 meters, Motorcycle wheelbase 1.5 meters, SUV wheelbase 3.0 meters.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: geoTouches
candidates.comment: A geo touches relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one boundary point but no interior points. Also called: borders, adjoins, meets at boundary. Examples: "Country A" geo touches "Country B", "Property Line 1" geo touches "Property Line 2", "Lake Shore" geo touches "Land Mass". Distinct from geoIntersects, which can share interior points.
